findings.publicHarvestQuestion: Does public harvest() lift it to Low? No. The 'denial' to third parties is self-remediable per call (exemptStrategies), simulated off-chain before broadcast, value-neutral, and ends with one owner call. Public reach widens who sees the revert, not what it costs.
findings.outsideC4JudgeView: QA/NC at best; a strict judge would call it admin misconfiguration (invalid). C4 grades Low and NC inside the same QA report, so the label affects only the Low/NC sub-grade, not inclusion.
findings.disagreementReason: Affirmatively justified, not a count-lowering downgrade: (1) the specific failure is documented by the team in three in-repo places, defeating the 'non-obvious' prong of the Law-3 footgun test that Low rests on; (2) fail-loud on an attended owner path with pre-broadcast simulation; (3) zero value at risk and per-call caller workaround. Recall is unaffected: the item stays in qa-report with its fix. Symmetry rule considered: understating here cannot leave a live exploit (no asset path exists), so the 'keep the higher when borderline' default does not bind with the same weight; the human may keep Low and nothing is lost either way.
findings.recommendedFinalSeverity: QA (non-critical), retained in qa-report.md; Low remains an acceptable ceiling at human triage.

findings.disclosureSentenceDraft: Prior awareness: the repository already records this router behaviour. `test/fork/MainnetRoutes.sol` L31-L32 notes that this Router NG rejects an ERC4626 redeem ("Bad swap type" for swap_type 9), and story-007 Background L21 repeats it (citing that file at L52; the note is now at L32). The shipped `ICurveRouterNG` NatSpec (L21-L22) states that unknown swap types revert "Bad swap type", and `test_fork_zeroSwapTypeOnExecutedHop_realRouterReverts_mockAgrees` (`test/fork/SYAHarvester.fork.t.sol` L528-L545) pins that revert on the real router for swap_type 0. The router behaviour is therefore known to the team; the gap is that `setRoute` enforces only the lower bound of the dispatch range (`!= 0`) and not the upper bound (`<= 8`), while its NatSpec says executed rows dispatch on a real swap_type.
findings.notes: Mechanics are correct and high-confidence; only the band is in question.
